items.title: Walmart Is Playing the Long Game by Lowering Prices
items.summary: Walmart’s finance chief had a message Thursday for analysts pressing the company on its decision to cut prices: Give it time.  Walmart  said it rolled back prices on more than 11,000 items, including ground beef, citing the ongoing strain on consumers of inflation and high gas prices.  The move comes after the company received tariff refunds worth about $2.9 billion, which it’s using to fund the price cuts.

items.title: Walmart’s E-Commerce Sales Rise as Deliveries Accelerate
items.summary: Walmart said its U.S. e-commerce sales rose 24% in the second quarter, with more than 40% sales growth in deliveries fulfilled at its stores.  CEO  John Furner  said  Walmart  has now expanded deliveries of 30 minutes or less into 38 U.S. markets.  The number of units delivered in less than half an hour has doubled in the current quarter from a year ago, and 70% of all e-commerce orders are getting delivered on the same day or better, CFO  John David Rainey  said.

items.title: The Week in Numbers: U.S. debt hits $40 trillion, Walmart's rare miss
items.summary:
STORY: From U.S. debt soaring higher to Walmart's rare sales miss...this is the Week in Numbers. 

:: The Week in Numbers 

:: $40 trillion

$40 trillion is how high total U.S. debt hit for the first time.

It drew warnings from analysts a fiscal crisis is developing.

That as growing costs for social safety-net programs and interest payments far exceed revenues held back by tax cuts.

U.S. debt has more than doubled in less than a decade, from just under $20 trillion when President Donald Trump was sworn in for the first time in January 2017.

:: 10%

As much as 10% is how far Walmart shares sank after its latest results.

The retail giant announced quarterly sales growth was well below analyst expectations.

Reuters Correspondent Nicholas Brown.

“Walmart's sales grew only 2.6% which is the the slowest pace of growth in about six years for them. It's the first time that they've met failed to meet analyst estimates for their sales in about five years. So, it's exceedingly rare for Walmart to miss.” 

The company said shoppers were likely being squeezed by high gasoline prices, raising concerns pressure on U.S. consumers is growing. 

:: 160%

Around 160% is how high Moderna shares soared this week.

Investors bought in after the drugmaker and Merck announced a successful cancer treatment.

They said a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine lowered the risk of recurrence and spread of melanoma in a late-stage trial.

Moderna said thousands of patients could benefit as soon as next year if regulators approve the vaccine.

:: $50 billion

And $50 billion is how much Chinese robotics firm Unitree was valued on its Shanghai stock debut.

The firm is one of the world's biggest producers of humanoid and quadruped robots. 

Unitree has drawn global attention for its robots that run, dance and perform martial arts and become a source of national pride in China.

It isn't the first Chinese humanoid robot maker to go public, but its debut is expected to kick off a range of domestic rivals preparing to come to market.
